e-5219.problem:
What is the equation of the ellipse given below?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095374/assets/57ec3c089f80e2d35d9b83f6791eefca9b452d933f82209ed434d35d77b78788.png)
e-5219.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\dfrac{(x-h)^2}{{a}^2}+\dfrac{(y-k)^2}{{b}^2}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(1,-1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(3,-1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(3,-1),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-4,0),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-0)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(-4,0),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=5,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-0)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{25}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Remember that the general equation of an ellipse centered at $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the ellipse is centered at $(1,2),$ the horizontal radius has length $a=3,$ and the vertical radius has length $b=2.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
